# Skill: sign in to CURA Healthcare with the account the caller names. The
# caller passes vault references (never literal values), so the same skill can
# sign in as the valid demo user or feed a wrong password to a negative case.
description: Open the CURA Healthcare login page and submit the given username and password. Params - user, password (pass vault references such as <<CURA_USER>>). Does not assert the outcome; the calling case does.
params: [user, password]
steps:
  - goto: "https://katalon-demo-cura.herokuapp.com/profile.php#login"
  - aiAssert: "The CURA Healthcare login form is shown with Username and Password fields and a Login button"
  - ai: "Type {{user}} into the Username field"
  - ai: "Type {{password}} into the Password field"
  - ai: "Click the Login button"
files.samples/tests/_hooks/sample-login-orange:

files.samples/tests/_profiles/sample-web-stric:
# Same sample web suites, with the page listeners turned into verdicts: a case
# fails when the page logs an uncaught error or a request it made fails, even
# if every assertion passed. Use it to show the difference between "the screen
# looked right" and "the page was healthy".
description: "Sample web suites with console and API checks as verdicts"
platform: web

options:
  assertEvidence: true
  consoleCheck: true
  # Only the app under test's own traffic is judged. the-internet embeds a
  # third-party analytics beacon whose host does not resolve on every network,
  # and a tracker outage is not the app failing. The match is a substring of
  # the whole URL and the beacon carries the page URL in its query, so the
  # entry is anchored on the scheme separator.
  network:
    domains:
      - "://the-internet.herokuapp.com/"
    failOn: 5xx

interactive:
  clarify: fail

allow:
  hosts:
    - the-internet.herokuapp.com
files.samples/tests/_profiles/sample-web.yaml:
# The profile the sample web suites were written for. Bind it on a run of any
# web sample folder: it keeps a screenshot for every assertion and grants the
# one outbound host a sample tool calls (the-internet status probe).
#
# The sample-table-compare tool needs no host here: it calls the platform's own
# /aivision/table-compare primitive on loopback, which is not egress.
description: "Sample web suites: assertion evidence on, the-internet status probe allowed"
platform: web

options:
  assertEvidence: true

interactive:
  clarify: fail

allow:
  hosts:
    - the-internet.herokuapp.com
files.samples/tests/_tools/sample-table-compar:
# Deterministic verdict over a sample-table-compare result: any shape difference or
# cell mismatch fails the step with the first offending cells named. The case
# must have saved the sample-table-compare result as `compare` first.
runtime: js-page
description: >-
  Fail on any shape difference or cell mismatch in the saved `compare` result
  (from the sample-table-compare tool), else report how many cells matched.
script: >-
  (() => { const r = {{(compare)}}; if (!r.ok) throw new Error('compare
  failed: ' + JSON.stringify(r)); if (!r.shapeOk) throw new Error('table shape
  differs: expected ' + r.expectedRows + 'x' + r.expectedCols + ', got ' +
  r.actualRows + 'x' + r.actualCols); if (r.mismatchCount !== 0) throw new
  Error(r.mismatchCount + ' cell mismatch(es), first: ' +
  JSON.stringify(r.mismatches.slice(0, 3))); return 'all ' + r.comparedCells +
  ' cells match (' + r.actualRows + ' rows x ' + r.actualCols + ' cols, header
  row included)'; })()

# Compare a captured table against a stored fixture, cell by cell, on the
# platform's own API. The case must save its capture as `captured` first
# (`$: save-as: captured`): `{{(captured)}}` below is a step-variable
# expression that resolves against the run's saved variables when the call is
# built, while `{{fixture}}` is a declared param the caller fills.
#
# This is a platform primitive (loopback + /aivision/table-compare), so it runs
# under any profile without an allow.hosts entry.
description: Compare the table saved as "captured" against _fixtures/<fixture>.json, cell by cell
params: [fixture]
request:
  method: POST
  url: http://127.0.0.1:5880/aivision/table-compare
  headers:
    content-type: application/json
    accept: application/json
  body: '{"fixture":"{{fixture}}","actual":{{(captured)}}}'
expect:
  status: [200]
timeout: 60000
files.samples/tests/_tools/sample-the-internet:
# A real outbound request, gated by the profile: the-internet serves a page
# that answers with exactly the status code in its path. A case calls this
# before it opens a browser to prove the app under test is reachable.
#
# Egress is deny-by-default, so this tool only runs on a profile that lists
# the-internet.herokuapp.com under allow.hosts (sample-web does).
description: GET the-internet's /status_codes/200 page and expect HTTP 200 — a reachability probe for the app under test.
request:
  method: GET
  url: https://the-internet.herokuapp.com/status_codes/200
  headers:
    accept: text/html
expect:
  status: [200]
timeout: 15000
files.samples/tests/sample-android/KB.md:
# sample-android — agent knowledge base

## Principles
- Assert on stable landmarks (a logo, a page heading, a menu label, the signed-in user's name), not on marketing copy. Wording drifts; landmarks stay.
- A step that types a value is done when the field holds it. Check the field, not the keystrokes.
- A disabled primary button means a prerequisite is missing: look for an empty required field, an unticked box or an unmade selection before clicking again.
- These cases drive apps that ship with every Android emulator image (Settings, Clock), so they need no app install.
- Run them on a booted Android emulator or a USB-connected phone. Test Management > Devices shows the health check and the next step when no device is ready.

## Tips
- Settings rows are stacked tightly. Name the exact row title in the step so a neighbouring row is not tapped.
- A screen that scans for something (Wi-Fi networks) fills in a moment after it opens; wait for the content before asserting.

## Known blockers

## Glossary

      - ai: "Tap the tab labelled 'Alarm' in the bottom navigation bar (the leftmost tab). Do not tap Bedtime."
      - aiAssert: "The Alarm tab is selected and a round add (+) button is visible above the tab bar"

# sample-bill-splitter — agent knowledge base

## Principles

# sample-cellphone — agent knowledge base

## Principles
- Assert on stable landmarks (a logo, a page heading, a menu label, the signed-in user's name), not on marketing copy. Wording drifts; landmarks stay.
- A step that types a value is done when the field holds it. Check the field, not the keystrokes.
- A disabled primary button means a prerequisite is missing: look for an empty required field, an unticked box or an unmade selection before clicking again.
- Cellphone Shop (cellphone-demo.aut.katalon.com) is a demo store. The cart lives in the browser session; a fresh session starts with an empty cart, and the counter next to the header cart button shows 0.
- The add-to-cart button on a product page is labelled Buy. Accessories come with a Color picker (e.g. Pink, Blue, Yellow) with nothing preselected: clicking Buy before picking a color only shows "Please, choose a variant." and adds nothing. Pick a color first, one click per step.

## Tips
- The header cart shows only an item count next to the cart icon, no total. Adding an item opens a 'Product added to cart' popup with the line total (e.g. $ 39.00 x 1 = $ 39.00).
- Prices are written with a space after the dollar sign: $ 39.00.
- Product cards on the home page show the name and the price; a sale item shows the old price struck through next to the new one — the new price is the one that is charged.

## Known blockers

## Glossary
- MagSafe: Apple's magnetic case standard; it appears in accessory names.
files.samples/tests/sample-cellphone/add-acces:
# labels: sample, smoke, cellphone, save-as
# Intent: adding an accessory to the cart confirms it at the price the product
# page showed. The price is read off the product page and saved, so the
# confirmation is checked against what the shop itself displayed.
web:
  url: https://cellphone-demo.aut.katalon.com/
cases:
  - name: "Adding the iPhone 15 Silicone Case confirms it in the cart"
    steps:
      - aiWaitFor:
          prompt: "The K Cellphone Shop home page is shown with its navigation bar and the cart button in the header"
          $:
            timeout: 90000
      - aiAssert: "The item counter next to the cart button in the header shows 0"
      - ai: "Scroll down to the product cards and click the one named 'iPhone 15 Silicone Case with Magsafe'"
      - aiAssert: "The product page for 'iPhone 15 Silicone Case with Magsafe' is shown with a price and a Buy button"
      - aiQuery:
          prompt: "The product's price exactly as shown on the product page, e.g. $ 39.00"
          $:
            save-as: price
      # Accessories have no color preselected: Buy only shows "Please, choose a
      # variant." until one is picked.
      - aiTap: "The Blue button in the Color picker"
      - aiTap: "The Buy button"
      - aiWaitFor:
          prompt: "A 'Product added to cart' popup is shown"
          $:
            timeout: 30000
      - aiAssert:
          prompt: "The 'Product added to cart' popup lists 'iPhone 15 Silicone Case with Magsafe' with a total of {{price}}, and the item counter next to the header cart button shows 1"
          $:
            dom-included: visible-only

# sample-cura — agent knowledge base

## Principles
- Assert on stable landmarks (a logo, a page heading, a menu label, the signed-in user's name), not on marketing copy. Wording drifts; landmarks stay.

- CURA Healthcare Service is a public demo appointment app. Booking an appointment does not persist across sessions; history only holds what this session booked.

## Tips
- The Facility field is a native dropdown: write the step as select "<facility>" in the Facility dropdown.

- Healthcare Program: the Medicare / Medicaid / None radio group on the appointment form.
files.samples/tests/sample-cura/book-appointme:
# labels: sample, cura, skill, native-select, save-as, hooks
# Intent: a signed-in patient books an appointment and the confirmation
# repeats exactly what was entered. The facility is set through the platform's
# deterministic native-select path; the visit date is picked on the calendar,
# read back with aiQuery, saved as a variable and spliced into the
# confirmation assertion.
web:
  url: https://katalon-demo-cura.herokuapp.com/
beforeEach:
  - use:
      name: sample-login-cura
      with:
        user: <<CURA_USER>>
        password: <<CURA_PASSWORD>>
  - aiAssert: "The Make Appointment page is shown"
afterEach:
  - ai: "Open the navigation menu with the toggle button in the top-right corner and click Logout"
cases:
  - name: "Booking an appointment shows a matching confirmation"
    steps:
      - ai: select "Hongkong CURA Healthcare Center" in the Facility dropdown
      - ai: "Tick the 'Apply for hospital readmission' checkbox"
      - ai: "Select the Medicaid radio button under Healthcare Program"
      - ai: "Click the Visit Date field, then click day 28 in the calendar that opens"
      - aiQuery:
          prompt: "The date shown in the Visit Date field, exactly as displayed (dd/mm/yyyy)"
          $:
            save-as: visitDate
      - ai: "Type 'Sample booking from AI Vision' into the Comment field"
      - ai: "Click the Book Appointment button"
      - aiAssert: "The Appointment Confirmation page is shown"
      - aiAssert:
          prompt: "The confirmation lists Facility 'Hongkong CURA Healthcare Center', Apply for hospital readmission 'Yes', Healthcare Program 'Medicaid' and Visit Date '{{visitDate}}'"
          $:
            dom-included: visible-only

# sample-orangehrm — agent knowledge base

## Principles
- Assert on stable landmarks (a logo, a page heading, a menu label, the signed-in user's name), not on marketing copy. Wording drifts; landmarks stay.
- A step that types a value is done when the field holds it. Check the field, not the keystrokes.
- A disabled primary button means a prerequisite is missing: look for an empty required field, an unticked box or an unmade selection before clicking again.
- This is the public OrangeHRM open-source demo. Anyone can edit its data, so assert on page structure (headings, menus, table columns), never on a specific employee or user record.
- The signed-in user is Admin. The user name shown in the top-right header changes whenever someone renames the account — do not assert on it.

## Tips
- The login form loads slowly after the page shell appears. Wait for the Username field before typing.
- The left side menu lists modules (Admin, PIM, Leave, Time, Recruitment, My Info, Performance, Dashboard, Directory, Maintenance, Claim, Buzz). Click the module name, not its icon.
- Search forms in Admin and PIM only apply after clicking the Search button; typing alone does not filter the table.

## Known blockers

## Glossary
- PIM: Personal Information Management — the employee list.
- System Users: the Admin module's list of login accounts.
files.samples/tests/sample-orangehrm/admin-use:
# labels: sample, orangehrm, skill, network, api-check
# Intent: the Admin user list is backed by a healthy users API, not just a
# table that happens to render. The sample-login-orangehrm skill does the setup; the
# network block and the apiExpect steps prove what the page actually sent.
web:
  url: https://opensource-demo.orangehrmlive.com/web/index.php/auth/login
network:
  domains:
    - opensource-demo.orangehrmlive.com
  fail-on: 5xx
  expect:
    - match: "/api/v2/admin/users"
      method: GET
      status: 200
      required: true
beforeEach:
  - use: sample-login-orangehrm
cases:
  - name: "Admin > System Users is backed by a healthy users API"
    steps:
      - ai: "In the left side menu, click Admin"
      - apiExpect:
          match: "/api/v2/admin/users"
          method: GET
          status: 200
          $:
            timeout: 20000
      - aiAssert: "The System Users page is shown with a Records Found count above a table of users"
      - ai: "Type Admin into the Username field of the System Users search form"
      - ai: "Click the Search button"
      - apiExpect:
          match: "/api/v2/admin/users"
          method: GET
          status: 200
          $:
            timeout: 20000
      - aiAssert: "The results table shows at least one record whose Username is Admin"

# sample-saucedemo — agent knowledge base

## Principles
- Assert on stable landmarks (a logo, a page heading, a menu label, the signed-in user's name), not on marketing copy. Wording drifts; landmarks stay.
- A step that types a value is done when the field holds it. Check the field, not the keystrokes.
- A disabled primary button means a prerequisite is missing: look for an empty required field, an unticked box or an unmade selection before clicking again.
- Swag Labs (www.saucedemo.com) is a demo store. The cart is kept per browser session; a fresh session starts with an empty cart and no badge on the cart icon.
- Demo users: standard_user works normally; locked_out_user is always refused. They all share one password, kept in the vault.

## Tips
- The cart icon is at the top right; its red badge shows the item count and disappears when the cart is empty.
- Checkout asks for First Name, Last Name and Zip/Postal Code before showing the overview.

## Known blockers

## Glossary
- inventory: the Products page listing.
files.samples/tests/sample-saucedemo/cart-and-:

# sample-the-internet — agent knowledge base

## Principles
- Assert on stable landmarks (a logo, a page heading, a menu label, the signed-in user's name), not on marketing copy. Wording drifts; landmarks stay.
- A step that types a value is done when the field holds it. Check the field, not the keystrokes.
- A disabled primary button means a prerequisite is missing: look for an empty required field, an unticked box or an unmade selection before clicking again.
- the-internet (the-internet.herokuapp.com) is a collection of small single-purpose pages, each reached from the home page's link list or directly by its path.
- Pages have no shared navigation bar. To reach another example, go back to the home page or open its path.

## Tips
- The Dropdown example is a native select: write the step as select "Option 2" in the dropdown.
- The Form Authentication page reports success or failure in a colored flash banner at the top of the page.

## Known blockers

## Glossary
- flash banner: the colored message box the-internet shows at the top of a page after a form is submitted.
files.samples/tests/sample-the-internet/checkb:
# labels: sample, smoke, the-internet, save-as, javascript
# Intent: clicking a checkbox flips its state. The state before the click is
# saved as a variable and the assertion after it is written against that
# saved value, so the case holds whatever the page starts with.
web:
  url: https://the-internet.herokuapp.com/checkboxes
cases:
  - name: "Clicking checkbox 1 flips its checked state"
    steps:
      - aiAssert: "The Checkboxes page is shown with two checkboxes"
      - javascript:
          script: "document.querySelectorAll('#checkboxes input')[0].checked"
          $:
            save-as: firstBefore
      - ai: "Click the first checkbox, labelled 'checkbox 1'"
      - javascript:
          script: "(() => { const now = document.querySelectorAll('#checkboxes input')[0].checked; if (now === {{firstBefore}}) throw new Error('checkbox 1 did not change: still ' + now); return now; })()"
      - aiAssert: "Checkbox 1 is {{firstBefore ? 'unchecked' : 'checked'}}"
files.samples/tests/sample-the-internet/dropdo:
# labels: sample, smoke, the-internet, native-select, javascript
# Intent: choosing an option in a native dropdown sticks. The select step takes
# the platform's deterministic path (no model call); a javascript step reads
# the real <select> value so the check does not rely on pixels alone.
web:
  url: https://the-internet.herokuapp.com/dropdown
cases:
  - name: "Selecting 'Option 2' in the dropdown keeps it selected"
    steps:
      - aiAssert: "The Dropdown List page is shown with a dropdown"
      - ai: select "Option 2" in the dropdown
      - javascript:
          script: "(() => { const s = document.querySelector('#dropdown'); const text = s.options[s.selectedIndex].text; if (text !== 'Option 2') throw new Error('dropdown shows ' + text); return text; })()"
      - aiAssert: "The dropdown shows 'Option 2' as the selected value"

files.samples/tests/sample-the-internet/tables:
# labels: sample, the-internet, tools, fixture, table-compare
# Intent: the Sortable Data Tables page renders Example 1 exactly as the stored
# fixture _fixtures/sample-the-internet-tables-example1.json says, cell by cell.
#
# How each lane contributes:
#   - the sample-the-internet-status tool (http, egress) proves the app is reachable
#     before any AI step runs. It needs the sample-web profile, which allows
#     the-internet.herokuapp.com.
#   - aiAssert (model) judges what a person sees.
#   - sample-capture-html-table (js-page tool) reads the table's cell text.
#   - sample-table-compare (platform primitive) diffs it against the fixture.
#   - sample-table-compare-verdict (js-page tool) turns the diff into pass/fail.
web:
  url: https://the-internet.herokuapp.com/tables
beforeAll:
  - tool:
      name: sample-the-internet-status
      label: "Check the-internet answers HTTP 200 before the case starts"
cases:
  - name: "Example 1 table matches the stored fixture cell by cell"
    steps:
      - aiAssert: "The Data Tables page is shown with an 'Example 1' table listing people with Last Name, First Name, Email, Due and Web Site columns"
      - tool:
          name: sample-capture-html-table
          label: "Capture the Example 1 table as rows of cell text"
          with:
            selector: "#table1"
          $:
            save-as: captured
      - tool:
          name: sample-table-compare
          with:
            fixture: sample-the-internet-tables-example1
          $:
            save-as: compare
      - tool:
          name: sample-table-compare-verdict
          label: "Verdict: fail on any shape difference or cell mismatch"
